sections.title: Risk Factors
text: An investment in our common stock involves significant risks. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, as well as the other information we have provided in this prospectus before you decide to invest in our common stock. If any of the following risks are realized, in whole or in part, our business, financial condition, operating results and prospects could be materially and adversely affected. In that event, the price of our common stock could decline, and you could lose part or all of your investment. The risks described are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently view as immaterial may also materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, operating results and prospects, as well as the value of our common stock. See also “Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements.”

If the market price of gold were to drop and the prices realized by us on gold sales were to decrease significantly and remain at such a level for any substantial period, our profitability and cash flow would be negatively affected.

Gold prices have fluctuated widely in recent years. These fluctuations can be material and can occur over short periods of time and are affected by numerous factors, all of which are beyond our control. Future production from our mining properties is dependent on gold prices that are adequate to make these properties economically viable. During 2025 and the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the market price of gold ranged from $2,615 per ounce to an all-time high of $5,405 per ounce. The average market price of gold in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $4,545 per ounce, an all-time average high and an increase of 32% compared to the 2025 annual average of $3,432 per ounce. sections.title: Business
text: American Barrick is a premier pure-play gold producer and the largest gold producer with a portfolio of assets located entirely in North America. We operate six large, high-quality assets in two jurisdictions, Nevada and the Dominican Republic, including every Tier One gold asset that exists in the United States and four of the world’s 16 largest gold assets by 2025 production. In 2025, we produced 2.0 million ounces (“Moz”) of gold on an attributable basis. Our portfolio is underpinned by 40 Moz of attributable mineral reserves, representing a 20-year reserve life, and 38 Moz of attributable mineral resources.

Our portfolio is anchored by our 61.5% joint venture interest in Nevada Gold Mines in the United States, the largest gold mining complex in the world and the centerpiece of the premier gold mining jurisdiction globally. Within Nevada Gold Mines, we are advancing the Fourmile project, which we believe is one of the most significant gold discoveries of the last 25 years. Fourmile represents a compelling source of future growth, integrated into the Cortez Complex and supported by Nevada Gold Mines’ existing infrastructure. Assuming Fourmile timely reaches its expected annual production run-rate, by 2034 we would own and operate five of the seven North American mines producing over 500 thousand ounces (“Koz”) per year.

Nevada Gold Mines is located in Nevada and accounted for 81% of our attributable gold production in 2025. Nevada is the world’s premier gold mining jurisdiction, ranked the #1 mining jurisdiction globally for investment attractiveness on the Fraser Institute’s 2025 survey and a top-three jurisdiction for nine consecutive years. The State of Nevada has contributed 72% of overall U.S. gold production since 2020 and is also the #2 gold mineral resource endowment on Earth, making it the most important and prospective geological land package in the Western Hemisphere.

sections.title: Properties
text: Our production and exploration properties are described below.

In August 2026, Barrick and Newmont entered into a settlement agreement with respect to the Nevada Gold Mines joint venture pursuant to which, among other things, Barrick agreed to contribute Fourmile, and Newmont agreed to contribute its Mike and Fiberline developments, into the joint venture. Under the settlement agreement, each of Newmont and Barrick agreed to release the other party from, and to waive and to not pursue, any and all claims based upon or relating to the Nevada Gold Mines joint venture and related disputes to the date of the settlement agreement. In addition, Newmont agreed to waive any and all rights it may have under the agreements governing the Nevada Gold Mines joint venture and the Pueblo Viejo joint venture, and to not pursue any adverse action, relating to or in connection with this offering and the related transactions. In connection with the settlement agreement, Barrick and Newmont also entered into the Second Amended and Restated NGM JV Agreement, a copy of which is included as Exhibit 10.9 to the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part. On , 2026, pursuant to the terms of the settlement agreement, Barrick contributed Fourmile, and Newmont contributed Mike and Fiberline developments, into the Nevada Gold Mines joint venture. In addition, Newmont made a cash payment in the amount of $1.95 billion to Barrick under the terms of the settlement agreement. After giving effect to such transactions, we continue to hold a 61.5% controlling interest in Nevada Gold Mines.

The Cortez Complex is located 100 kilometers southwest of the town of Elko, Nevada in the Lander and Eureka Counties at elevations ranging from 1,370 meters to 1,675 meters. The boundaries of the Cortez operational areas encompass approximately 31,889 hectares. As of December 31, 2025, Cortez employed approximately 1,650 employees and averaged approximately 300 contractors. …

Mark Hill will be the President and Chief Executive Officer and a member of the board of directors of the Company upon completion of this offering. Prior to this role, Mr. Hill has served as President, Chief Executive Officer and Director of Barrick since February 2026. Mr. Hill will resign these positions at Barrick in connection with the completion of this offering. Mr. Hill also served as Group Chief Operating Officer and Interim President and Chief Executive Officer of Barrick from September 2025 to February 2026, as Chief Operating Officer, Latin America and Asia Pacific from May 2020 to September 2025 and Chief Operating Officer, LATAM and Australia Pacific from January 2019 to May 2020. Mr. Hill is a seasoned mining executive with 30 years of experience. He joined Barrick in 2006 and has experience in strategy, corporate development and leading major projects across the world. He was also integral in the initial decision to undertake exploration at the Fourmile gold project in Nevada. Mr. Hill holds an undergraduate degree in mining engineering from Ballarat University and a graduate diploma in mineral economics from Macquarie University. We believe that Mr. Hill is qualified to serve as a member of our board of directors because of his extensive senior management experience and leadership experience in the mining industry, including at Barrick, and his deep operational and strategic expertise developed over 30 years in the mining sector.

On December 1, 2025, the Board of Directors of Barrick Mining Corporation (“Barrick” or the “Parent”) authorized the management team to commence preparation for an initial public offering (“IPO”) of Barrick’s North American gold assets. North American Barrick (“we”, “our”, or the “Business”) represents those North American assets and investments owned directly and indirectly by Barrick that are proposed to be separated from the existing group. The Business is principally engaged in the production and sale of gold, as well as related activities such as exploration and mine development. We sell our gold production into the world market.

The primary businesses included in these carve-out financial statements are Barrick’s 61.5% interest in Nevada Gold Mines in Nevada, USA, comprised of the Carlin, Cortez, Turquoise Ridge and Phoenix producing gold mines, as well as the formerly producing Long Canyon gold mine; Barrick’s 60% interest in Pueblo Viejo, a producing gold mine in the Dominican Republic; and the 100% owned Fourmile exploration-stage gold project in Nevada, USA. Subsequent to December 31, 2025, Barrick entered into an agreement with Newmont Corporation (“Newmont”) to contribute Fourmile to Nevada Gold Mines, which would result in the Business holding a 61.5% interest in Fourmile through its interest in Nevada Gold Mines. We expect the contribution to occur in the fourth quarter of 2026. Refer to note 23 for further information. We also have various projects and exploration tenements located throughout the USA, Canada and the Caribbean.

These carve-out financial statements have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). Accounting policies are consistently applied to all years presented, unless otherwise stated. …

The inherent uncertainty of mineral reserve and mineral resource estimates, which may differ materially from actual results, and the need to replace depleted mineral reserves;

The impact of government controls, regulations and tax laws on our operations;
Extensive permitting requirements and the risk of failure to obtain or maintain required permits;

Political, economic and legal risks associated with our operations in the Dominican Republic, or other foreign countries we may invest in, including expropriation, changes in tax or royalty regimes and civil disturbances;
Significant physical risks and hazards inherent in mining, including equipment failures, tailings dam failures, seismic activity and the potential insufficiency of insurance coverage;
Pending and potential disputes, litigation and other legal proceedings;
Risks inherent in our joint ventures, including potential misalignment with partners;
Supply chain disruptions, commodity shortages and labor constraints that could increase costs or delay operations;
Concentration of our operations within the Nevada Gold Mines Complex and the Pueblo Viejo mine, which limits our ability to offset adverse developments at either location;
The impact of international trade policies, including tariffs, on our costs for raw materials, components and equipment;
Competition for mining claims, properties, infrastructure, key personnel and access to water and power;
Work stoppages, labor disputes, contractor reliance and health and safety incidents;
Changes in tax laws, including the adoption of a global minimum tax, and exposures to additional tax liabilities that could adversely affect our effective tax rate and financial condition;
Tax audits, reviews and examinations by authorities in the jurisdictions in which we operate, which could result in material tax liabilities in excess of reserves;

The impact of our indebtedness on our financial flexibility, including our ability to obtain additional financing and our vulnerability to adverse economic conditions and restrictions on our operational flexibility;
Not realizing the anticipated benefits from the Separation and unforeseen harms associated with the Separation;
The complexity of the Separation transactions and the potential for delayed or incomplete asset and liability transfers;

Restrictions on our ability to raise capital, make acquisitions or issue equity incentives in order to preserve Barrick’s ability to effect a tax-free distribution of shares of our common stock, which could limit our ability to grow;
Actual or potential conflicts of interest among certain of our directors and officers due to their equity ownership in, or positions with, Barrick;
The potential insufficiency of Barrick’s indemnification obligations and the risk of substantial indemnification claims against us;
Barrick’s control of our business as our majority stockholder, whose interests may not align with those of our other stockholders;
Volatility in the market price of our common stock due to factors including gold price changes, analyst coverage and actions by Barrick;
Our status as a “controlled company” under NYSE rules, which permits us to rely on exemptions from certain corporate governance requirements; and

The potential for sales or distributions of shares of our common stock by our stockholders (including by Barrick, our executive officers or our directors following the expiration of lock-up agreements) that may depress our share price.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text:
Capital expenditures are classified into minesite sustaining capital expenditures or project capital expenditures depending on the nature of the expenditure. Minesite sustaining capital expenditures is the capital spending required to support current production levels. Project capital expenditures represent the capital spending at new projects and major, discrete projects at existing operations intended to increase net present value through higher production or longer mine life. Management believes these to be useful indicators of the purpose of capital expenditures and this distinction is an input into the calculation of all-in sustaining costs per ounce.

Classifying capital expenditures is intended to provide additional information only and does not have any standardized definition under GAAP, and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for measures of performance prepared in accordance with GAAP. Other companies may calculate these measures differently.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text:
General and administrative expenses consist of allocations from Barrick related to items such as shared services, centralized functions, or corporate overhead. Allocations were determined by management on a reasonable and consistent basis using metrics that reflect the cost of our business, such as operating costs and capital expenditures.

For the six months ended June 30, 2026, general and administrative expenses decreased by $7 million compared to the six months ended June 30, 2025 mainly due to lower corporate administration expenses.

General and administrative expenses in 2025 increased by $47 million compared to 2024 due to higher stock-based compensation due to a significant increase in Barrick’s share price.

General and administrative expenses in 2024 decreased by $10 million compared to 2023 due to lower corporate administration expenses attributed to reductions in employee and consultant costs, combined with lower stock-based compensation expense as a result of a decrease in Barrick’s share price.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense, Net
nonop.text:
• Includes non-cash interest expense relating to the streaming agreement with Royal Gold Inc. (“Royal Gold”) in respect of Pueblo Viejo (as further described in “Business—Reportable Operating Segments-Pueblo Viejo (60% basis)”) of approximately $12 million and $14 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and approximately $18 million, $28 million and $27 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

For the six months ended June 30, 2026, interest expense, net was $7 million lower than for the six months ended June 30, 2025 as a result of higher capitalized interest primarily relating to the Ren project at Carlin, combined with lower non-cash interest expense relating to the Pueblo Viejo streaming agreement with Royal Gold.

In 2025, interest expense, net was 3% higher than 2024, primarily due to lower capitalized interest relating to the Pueblo Viejo expansion project, partially offset by lower non-cash interest expense relating to the streaming agreement with Royal Gold.

In 2024, interest expense, net was 9% higher than 2023, primarily due to lower capitalized interest relating to the Pueblo Viejo expansion project.
